2.x: **Brokers:** **Tilak and Jinnah**; Besant also helped; Sarojini Naidu called Jinnah the "Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity".
**Main concession:** the **Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims** – the **first time (1916)** the Congress did so; Muslims got a **fixed proportion of seats** (weightage).

**Joint demands:** self-government at an early date; expanded councils with **elected majorities** (also in the provincial councils); **half** of the executive councils to be Indians; five-year council term; Secretary of State paid from the British treasury; separation of the executive from the judiciary.
**Communal veto:** no bill affecting a community could pass if **three-fourths** of that community's members opposed it.
**Not in the Pact:** no merger (separate sessions continued), no power-sharing deal, no demand for complete independence.
**Unity period:** **1916-1922** (Lucknow Pact → Khilafat-Non-Cooperation) – the high point of Congress-League unity.
**Order:** **Muslim League (1906) → Morley-Minto (1909) → Lucknow Pact (Dec 1916) → Jallianwala Bagh (13 Apr 1919) → Tilak's death (1 Aug 1920) → Swaraj Party (1 Jan 1923)**.
Lucknow 1916: Congress president **A.C. Majumdar**, League president **Jinnah**; the Congress **accepted** separate electorates.

3.x: **Stated reason:** protecting the Muslim minority. **Real reason:** part of the British policy of **divide and rule** – to set Muslims against the Congress and maintain British supremacy.
**Effects:** checked India's unification, encouraged separatism, became a potent factor in the **growth of communalism** – the "seeds of discord" that ended in partition.
**Lord Minto** = "**Father of the Communal Electorate**" – used separate electorates to **turn Muslims against the Congress**.
Separate electorates = Minto (1909); Congress accepted them = Lucknow (1916).
